name: Supplier bank account change
red_flags: Asks you to send payment to a new bank account
Creates urgency to pay before you can verify the change
Impersonates a supplier or business contact you already trust
safe_steps: Do not send any payment to the new account yet
Call your supplier using a number you already have on file — not one from this message
If you already paid, contact your bank immediately to try to stop or reverse the transfer

name: Fake SAT fine or mailbox notice
red_flags: Claims to be from SAT (Mexico's tax authority) with a mailbox notice or fine
Pressures you to pay quickly through a link to avoid a penalty
SAT does not request payment through WhatsApp or SMS links
safe_steps: Do not click the link or pay anything from this message
Check your real SAT mailbox directly at sat.gob.mx, not through this link
If unsure, call SAT's official line or ask your accountant to verify

name: Fake vehicle plate fine
red_flags: Claims your vehicle plates have an unpaid fine or infraction
Includes a link to "pay now" to avoid towing or further penalties
Real traffic fines are not usually sent with urgent payment links by SMS or WhatsApp
safe_steps: Do not pay through the link in this message
Check your fines directly on your state or city's official traffic authority website
If you're unsure, visit an official module in person or call the official traffic hotline

name: Fake delivery fee or wrong address
red_flags: Claims a package can't be delivered because of a wrong address or unpaid fee
Asks for a small payment through a link to "release" or reschedule delivery
Creates urgency around a package you may not be expecting
safe_steps: Do not pay through the link in this message
Check your order status directly on the courier's official website or app, not through this link
If you weren't expecting a package, treat this as a scam and delete it

name: Fake bank security alert
red_flags: Claims suspicious activity on your account and asks you to "confirm" a code
A real bank never asks you to share a one-time code or password by message
Threatens that your account will be blocked if you don't respond quickly
safe_steps: Never share a code, password, or PIN with anyone, even if they say they're your bank
Stop responding, then call your bank using the number on the back of your card
Report the message to your bank's fraud line

name: Family emergency / new number scam
red_flags: A supposed family member or friend claims to be texting from a new number
Asks for money urgently, often for an emergency, bail, or medical bill
Asks you to keep it secret or not call anyone to verify
safe_steps: Do not send any money yet
Call your family member or friend directly at the number you already had for them
If you can't reach them, call another relative to verify before sending anything

name: Fake job offer or prize
red_flags: Offers a job or prize that seems too good to be true
Asks you to pay a deposit, fee, or "registration" before you receive anything
A legitimate employer or prize never asks you to pay money first
safe_steps: Do not send any payment or deposit
Research the company or offer independently before responding
If it asks for money upfront, treat it as a scam

name: Fake invoice or CFDI download
red_flags: Asks you to download an attached "invoice" or CFDI file from an unexpected sender
The download link or file may contain malware
Real invoices from known suppliers usually arrive through expected, verified channels
safe_steps: Do not download or open the attachment
Confirm with the sender directly, using a phone number or email you already know, before opening anything
If you already downloaded it, run an antivirus scan and avoid opening the file
